_comment: Reviewer overrides on the computed sector layer, per sector. Two kinds, in one file
because they are the same idea: the model is not the last word, and it should not
pretend to be.
`overrides` — the measure RANKING.
A reviewer reading the sector reads things the model has no parameter for. An
override is allowed and is never silent: `rank` and `reason` are both rendered on
the measure page, next to the computed components they displace, so a reader can
see exactly where the machine stopped and a person started.
sources/check_importance.py fails the build on a rank without a reason. That is the
only rule: an override with a stated reason is legitimate, an override without one
is the ranking being quietly edited.
Shape:  { "<sector>": { "<file>:<id>": { "rank": 1, "reason": "..." } } }
Empty on purpose. Cement's first ranking has not been reviewed yet.
`summary_overrides` — the LEAD SENTENCE and WHY IT MATTERS.
sources/build_lead.py generates both from the sector's own panels. A reviewed
sentence here replaces the generated one, renders identically — unsigned, per
amendment brief 2 §4 — and carries the date it was read.
`fingerprint` is the build's hash of the facts the sentence was written against.
When the facts move, the build sets `override_stale`, prints, and KEEPS RENDERING
the reviewed sentence. Reverting to generated text on a fingerprint change would
silently discard reviewed prose, which is the exact failure the review rule exists
to prevent; showing reviewed prose with a flag on the build is the lesser one.
Shape:  { "<sector>": { "sentence": "...", "why_it_matters": "...",
"from": ["<fact id>", ...], "reviewed": "YYYY-MM-DD",
"fingerprint": "<from data/transition/lead/<sector>.json>" } }
Empty on purpose. The first candidate for cement is the drafted sentence sitting
in data/prose.json under transition_notes — written for the old one-sentence lead,
never approved, and superseded by the generated lead. It is George's to approve,
rewrite, or drop.
